what: The plugin compiles in the vxl project: all four modules, with UHT on the USTRUCTs (FUniCoord, FUniCellKey, FUniObjectId) and the UFUNCTION library.
UE Automation tests (UnifiedUniverse.*) pass headless with -nullrhi, including engine-parity checks of the UniSeed port against ProcSeed / HashCombine / FRandomStream.
Every .usf entry point compiles under the engine shader compiler (DXC was not runnable here).
GPU execution parity: the shared cores give the same results on the GPU as their CPU runs through UniHlslShim.h (integer cores bitwise, float cores statistically, D-105).
Render hooks: the scene view extension subscribes at the intended points on the project's engine version (D-006), and sprites appear with scene-depth occlusion.
Flythrough in the editor: `uu.Flythrough` console command on an empty level shows the backdrop, with no jitter and no pops.

Promotion handoff appearance: the reference renderer showed the sprite's glare far larger than the promoted body (OBSERVATIONS.md). In UE there is no promotion actor pool yet, so promoted stars stay sprites; check how the glare reads with real bloom.

Runtime cost: GPU time of the generate / project / sprite passes, the one-time game-thread hitch of the normalising integral when entering a galaxy (D-123), and teleport fill latency (about 37 frames, D-122).

The volume pass in the engine (Docs/VOLUMETRICS.md §8) is written but has never been compiled: UniVolume.usf (MarchCS, BackgroundCS, CompositeVS/PS), the sprite transmittance lookup, RenderVolume_RenderThread and the subsystem's per-frame volume scene. It must compile, show the galaxy glow and the dust lane matching the reference stills, and stay within budget (uu.Volume 0/1 to compare).

Star systems in the engine (D-142 to D-145): the activation append and readback ring in UniProject.usf / RenderBackdrop_RenderThread, the planet-record scatter into the reserved pool tail, the subsystem's clock and system manager. Planets must appear near uu.GotoSystem, move with uu.TimeScale, and activate/deactivate without flicker (REVIEW_TONIGHT §9).

M3 in the engine (D-146, D-147): UUniParallaxComponent placement (real space vs compressed, no jitter against the backdrop at any speed), AUniBodyActor placeholders spawned and destroyed on promotion, promoted planets' sprites culled, the light rig, and sprites hidden behind promoted bodies by the decoded depth test (REVIEW_TONIGHT §10).

Galaxy clusters and travel sensitivity in the engine (D-151 to D-154): the 208-byte task struct with sampling boxes and the cluster envelope bound on the GPU, uu.Cluster.* tuning, uu.Clusters / uu.GotoCluster, residency (~14k clusters) and game-thread cost, and the speed-driven sensitivity (REVIEW_TONIGHT §11).

Sprite style, instrumentation and volume cost in the engine (D-156, D-157): the 64-byte sprite with core + halo, uu.Sprite.* handles, uu.Perf / uu.PerfHud / uu.PerfHitchMs and the Insights scopes, the cluster step hint's GPU cost, the volume quality CVars (REVIEW_TONIGHT §12).

The web texture in the engine (D-164): the include of UniWebTexture.ush in every .usf, the Texture3D + wrap/trilinear sampler bound to the generation probe/place passes and the volume passes, the upload compute pass (UniWebTexUpload.usf), the bake/cache in Saved/UnifiedUniverse, uu.WebSource / uu.WebTexSize, and the GPU cost of Uni.Volume.Background with it (REVIEW_TONIGHT §13).

Contributors woken by distance at intergalactic speed in the engine (D-168): game-thread cost with uu.Enable flythrough from rest to ~100 Mpc/s with travel sensitivity (Measure, Wake, Register, Window in the hitch line), WakeTheta from the renderer's pixel angle, no missing stars or glow while moving (REVIEW_TONIGHT §13e).

Galaxy groups and dwarfs in the engine (D-174): groups resident from the node list, uu.GotoGroup [rich] landing at a group with its dwarfs and the web's bright galaxies around it, uu.Clusters listing clusters and groups from resident objects, uu.Group.Enable / uu.Group.Dwarfs, and no game-thread or GPU cost visible from groups (REVIEW_TONIGHT §13j).

The hybrid cluster split and map dwarfs in the engine (D-176, D-177): game-thread cost at intergalactic speed with uu.Enable flythrough and travel sensitivity (hitch lines: Submit, Levels, Wake; AwakeByAngle and WakeStep), clusters looking as before up close (uu.GotoCluster rich: bright members around the core, ellipticals in it), uu.GotoGroup and uu.Clusters finding groups (labels, no emitter), dwarfs clumped on nodes (REVIEW_TONIGHT §13k).

Galaxy disc modes in the engine (D-178): the 128-byte field parameters and 272-byte generation task on the GPU (automation struct sizes, placement unchanged in kind), rolled warps, lopsidedness and uneven arms visible on galaxies at a few degrees, the Milky Way band as before with a gentle outer warp (REVIEW_TONIGHT §14).
